title: Client Services Guidance — Signing, Lapse and the Initial Cost Deposit under the Legal Forwarding Agreements
content:
Under the Legal Forwarding Agreements, an agreement is issued to the creditor client for signature and stands as pending signature until it is signed or lapses. The rules that govern that period are these.

## The rule

> The agreement binds only on the client's signature. An agreement is signed only when the handling date is no later than the last day of the signature window counted from its issue date. The signature window is the programme's signature window in calendar days, the day after the issue date being day one and the last day included. Where the programme's required cost deposit is above $0.00, no account is forwarded until that deposit has been received. An unsigned agreement lapses on the first day after the window.

## The window broken down

| Element | How it is fixed |
|---|---|
| Starting point | the issue date shown on the agreement in Ridgeline's records |
| Day one | the calendar day after the issue date |
| Length | the forwarding programme's signature window, counted in calendar days |
| Last day | the day whose count equals the window length; it is inside the window |
| Signing allowed | on any handling date up to and including the last day |
| Lapse | on the first day after the last day, if still unsigned |

On signature the agreement moves from pending signature to active. If the window passes unsigned, the agreement lapses and its status becomes terminated, the termination date being the first day after the window.

## Boundary cases on hypothetical dates

The dates and window lengths below are invented to show the count.

**Case 1 — a 30-day window.** An agreement issued on 1 March: day one is 2 March and day 30 is 31 March.

| Handling date | Signature accepted? | Status that results |
|---|---|---|
| 31 March (the last day) | Yes — no later than the last day | active |
| 1 April (the day after) | No — later than the last day | the agreement lapses on 1 April, unsigned |

**Case 2 — a 45-day window.** An agreement issued on 1 March: 2 to 31 March are days one to 30, and 1 to 15 April are days 31 to 45, so the last day is 15 April. A signature on 15 April is accepted; on 16 April it is not, and 16 April is the lapse date.

## The initial cost deposit

The signature makes the agreement binding, but where the client's programme requires a cost deposit above $0.00, no account is forwarded until that deposit has been received — Ridgeline's records show the deposit received for the agreement. Where the programme's required deposit is $0.00, this rule does not hold forwarding back.

| Programme's required cost deposit | Deposit received? | May an account be forwarded under this rule? |
|---|---|---|
| Above $0.00 | No | No |
| Above $0.00 | Yes | This rule no longer stands in the way |
| $0.00 | — | This rule does not apply |

## Points of judgement

- *Does an agreement bind once it is issued?* No. It binds only on the client's signature.
- *What date governs the window?* The agreement's issue date in Ridgeline's records; the window is counted from the day after it.
- *Is the last day of the window still in time?* Yes. The last day is included.
